channel.title: Wire — AI
channel.description: AI from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Hacking OpenAI
item.description: A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repositories (2 sources: hackernews, lobsters)

item.title: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems
item.description: On May 11th, 2026, hundreds of malicious packages were uploaded to RubyGems by AI agents performing web-lookup tasks with significant overlap with the German Wiki Incident. (3 sources: hackernews, lobsters, rubyweekly)

item.title: Microsoft exec called AI scraping 'the largest theft of labor in human history'
item.description: Newly unsealed court filings show Microsoft privately called OpenAI's data practices "theft" while both companies scraped paywalled Times content, built datasets from it, and warned internally it would gut publishers. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Sex, AI, and the Apocalypse
item.description: How a community devoted to thinking clearly incubated salvation stories, abusive experiments, race science, and an affection for autocracy, and why that history matters now that its alumni are asking for the public trust on AI. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Show HN: Share your AI Setup, Learn from others
item.description: Discover how people work with AI, and follow what changes. Explore their setups and share your own. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: WSO2 Releases Agent Manager as Enterprises Look to Control Growing AI Agent Sprawl
item.description: WSO2 has announced the general availability of WSO2 Agent Manager, an open-source platform designed to provide centralized governance, identity management, security controls, and operational oversight for AI agents running across different… (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Presentation: Complexity and Creativity in Software Engineering
item.description: Phillip Mortimer discusses the shift toward write-only software driven by AI code generation. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Podcast: Signals and Levers: Building Thriving Engineering Organizations
item.description: In this podcast Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods spoke to Elisabeth Hendrickson and Joel Tosi about systems thinking as a lens for software delivery, the cultural "levers" leaders and teams can pull to shape organizations,… (1 source: infoq)

item.title: OpenAI Introduces Triage Framework and Case Studies to Report Model Misalignment
item.description: OpenAI has released a disclosure framework for model misalignment during its lifecycle. Employees can flag potential issues, prompting technical staff to label incidents. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: What is still exciting in tech?
item.description: A comment on a lobste.rs post about the tech culture stagnating made me think. 20-15 or even 10 years ago, tech was really exciting. Sure, monopolies were bad, I was fighting them, but tech by itself was very interesting. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: On learning programming in an age of LLMs
item.description: Open answers to a reader's letter. (1 source: lobsters)
